title: Adaptive harmonic slot scheduler for turn-size variance
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: On mixed prompt/response workloads (conversational apps with short prompts + long completions and vice versa), the continuous batcher produces slot fragmentation and aggressive KV cache churn that increases tail latency and causes GPU memory hotspots. Observed symptoms include p99 spikes during interleaved short/long sequences, kv eviction thrashing, and occasional OOMs on hot GPUs when many long-turn requests are admitted together.

Goal: Implement an adaptive slot scheduling algorithm that smooths slot tenure by using a harmonic-length weighting heuristic to favor slots that preserve coalescing across mixed turn sizes, combined with soft KV pinning and micro-slab defragmentation to reduce fragmentation and lower p99 latency without materially hurting throughput or average latency.

Scope: Scheduler + admission control + KV residency hints + monitoring. No changes to model kernels or quantization in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency on mixed-turn production-like replay reduced by >= 15% versus baseline
KV cache churn (evictions/sec) reduced by >= 20% on replay traces
Feature gated behind runtime flag and gradual rollout plan defined
tasks: Design harmonic weighting algorithm and slot-age smoothing (initial design doc)
Implement scheduler prototype in continuous-batcher module
Add soft KV pinning heuristics and micro-slab defrag hook
Instrumentation: add per-slot residency counters, kv-hit/eviction metrics, GPU slab fragmentation metrics
Create replay tests (short/long interleaved traces) and load harness
Run perf experiments and capture baseline vs candidate metrics
Code review and iterate based on infra/ops feedback
Feature-flag rollout: canary -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback
design_notes: Harmonic weighting: compute harmonic mean of recent length samples per cohort to bias slot assignment toward minimizing large variance within a slot. This reduces cross-turn preemption and preserves KV locality.
Slot-age smoothing: introduce exponential decay on slot priorities so recently-coalesced slots get short-term protection; prevents starvation via periodic global rebalancing checkpoint.
KV soft pinning: mark top-K hot prefixes with residency hint to avoid eviction unless memory pressure is critical; eviction can ignore soft-pinned entries until a high watermark.
Micro-slab defrag: scheduler emits low-priority background passes to compact KV slabs when GPU is underutilized for >200ms windows; knobs to tune duration and aggressiveness.
Admission control: add dynamic admission threshold that reduces acceptance of long-turn requests when average slot occupancy > 85% or slab fragmentation > threshold.
Compatibility: fall back to existing continuous-batcher policy when harmonic scheduler disabled. No breaking of RPC surface.
Trade-offs: biasing slots to reduce variance may slightly reduce peak throughput in highly uniform workloads; mitigated via runtime tuning and cohort-specific parameters.
experiments_plan: Benchmarks: run 3 replay suites: conversational mix A (70% short prompts, 30% long completions), mix B (50/50), and edge mix C (many interleaved long+short).
Baseline: collect p50/p95/p99 latencies, kv-hit-rate, evictions/sec, GPU memory free fragmentation metric, tokens/sec for baseline config (current master).
Candidate: run harmonic scheduler + kv-pin + micro-defrag with a sweep over harmonic window sizes [8,16,32] and pin-K [16,64].
Statistical plan: 10 runs each scenario, compute median and 95% confidence intervals; require consistent improvement across mixes before rollout.
A/B runtime canary: route 5% of production traffic for 48h with metric checks for error rate, p99, and OOMs; automated rollback if any safety thresholds hit.
implementation_notes: Files touched: continuous_batcher/scheduler.py, continuous_batcher/kv_manager.cc, runtime/flags.rs, telemetry/metrics_registry.py
API surface: add SlotHint struct (cohort_id, harmonic_length, age_score) but keep serialized wire format backward compatible (unused by older nodes).
Perf considerations: harmonic weighting computation must be O(1) amortized per request; maintain sliding window counters instead of per-token loops.
Testing: unit tests for harmonic mean estimator, integration tests for slot re-assignment, stress test harness for OOM reproduction.
monitoring_and_alerts: Dashboards: create 'harmonic-scheduler' dashboard with p50/p95/p99, kv-evictions/sec, kv-hit-rate, slab-fragmentation, tokens/sec, OOM occurrences.
Alerts: fire if p99 increases > 20% for 10 minutes or kv-evictions/sec increases > 2x baseline or any OOM observed on canary nodes.
SLO experiment tag: tag canary traffic with experiment id 'hs-2026-02' for tracing and postmortem correlation.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Harmonic bias may cause unfairness for extremely long-turn heavy customers. Mitigation: cohort-level override to disable harmonic scheduling for customer-tagged requests.
Risk: Soft pinning could cause memory pressure in burst scenarios. Mitigation: two-tier pin (soft -> hard) with strict high-water eviction that ignores soft pins when critical.
Risk: Background micro-defrag passes may compete for GPU cycles. Mitigation: schedule defrag only during low-utilization windows and cap work per GPU per second.
Risk: Undetected regressions in uniform workloads. Mitigation: run synthetic uniform load regression tests during CI and require no regressions before merge.
